Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

investigate verb

also investigation, inquiry, inquire into, look into, hold an inquiry, investigator, track down, check (investigate), check out (inquire into), trace, track, track down something, trace back

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 119: dē morte alicujus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 1.27: dē pecūniīs repetundīs

quaerō, quaerere, quaesīvī, quaesītum

verb, third conjugation: in this sense with dē + ablative of the matter

inquire into, investigate

The classical word for an official inquiry: quaerere dē a death, a theft, a charge. The inquiry itself is quaestiō (quaestiōnem habēre dē, see trial). Its everyday senses are to look for and to ask (see look-for).

Other words

  • investīgō, investīgāre, investīgāvī, investīgātum — track down, search out

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.158 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 195, 334; Traupman 195; Traupman 289

    Properly to track, as a hound follows a scent (Cic. N.D. 2.158); then to trace or find out facts. Traupman gives it, and investīgātor, for investigate and investigator. See also research.

  • inquīrō, inquīrere, inquīsīvī, inquīsītum — search into, look into

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 289

    To search into a matter; in the courts, of a prosecutor gathering evidence against someone (in aliquem).

  • indāgō, indāgāre, indāgāvī, indāgātum — track down, trace (as a hound tracks)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.40: ad indāgandum canem (Lewis & Short s.v. ad); Cic. Tusc. 5.64: indāgāvī sepulcrum; Traupman 110, 397

  • investīgātor, investīgātōris m. — an investigator

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sull. 85: conjūrātiōnis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 193, 195

  • scrūtor, scrūtārī, scrūtātus sum — search thoroughly, examine

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Lewis & Short: “to search carefully, examine thoroughly, explore”; Traupman 289

  • repetō, repetere, repetīvī, repetītum — trace back (to its origin); go back over

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 35.28: viam, quā vēnisset, to retrace one’s way (Lewis & Short); Traupman 397

    Of a story or an argument, ab ultimō repetere is to go back to the very beginning.

Examples

  • Dē hāc rē quaerendum est.

    This needs looking into.composed

  • aliquid indāgāre

    to track something downTraupman 397

See also research, trial, evidence, suspect, murder, police.
